column5: finding

MCP server page inspected: hosted workspace endpoint /mcp; OAuth recommended with dynamic client registration or Bearer API key; read/write CRM access. This confirms MCP/auth path, not full plan or every tool permission.

Authentication page inspected: OAuth2; app registration required; server-side/client-side/user-password/app-auth flows; app-auth suitable for automated scripts. MCP endpoint was not page-inspected in this pass.

OAuth flow page inspected and API reference exposes broad CRM resources including leads, people, companies, opportunities, projects, tasks, activities, tags and custom fields. Exact credential eligibility and MCP not established in this pass.
MCP page inspected: open beta; remote Streamable HTTP endpoint; OAuth 2.1 + PKCE; confidential client required (no DCR); per-user permissions; read/write/send scopes.

Authentication page inspected: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code and client-credentials flows; app must be created in account; credentials tied to active invited user. Does not independently verify MCP scope/tool inventory.
REST API page inspected: REST/JSON API; API User permission must be granted by Gladly administrator before user can create API tokens; broad customer profile/timeline/order data. Sandbox described.
OAuth v2 page inspected: OAuth 2.0 installation, granular bot/user scopes and user approval; app gets token to call API methods/events. This does not verify MCP server feature coverage.
OAuth2 page inspected: authorization-code, implicit, client-credentials and bot/webhook flows; some scopes require Discord approval.
Telegram Login/OIDC authorization page inspected; it describes website/app login authorization, not the Telegram Bot API auth model. Do not use it alone to claim Bot API OAuth.

REST API auth page inspected: Basic Auth with dashboard-generated API ID/token for private/internal integrations; OAuth for multi-customer/public integrations; public integrations require approved tech-partner status.

Server-auth page inspected: Network Features flow requires enabled capability and valid JWT associated with an approved app; then authorization ID and CAMARA access token. This is a product-specific flow, not a complete survey of all Vonage APIs.

OAuth 2.0 page inspected: Authorization Code only for its external-auth configuration; user installs app and authorizes; platform stores access/refresh tokens. Distinguish this from HighLevel's own marketplace app API.

Authentication page inspected: private keys for server-side APIs; public key for client-side endpoints; OAuth recommended for tech partners; private keys can have read-only/custom/full scopes and key creation requires Owner/Admin/Manager role.
v3 API authentication page inspected: broad REST v3 API reference; auth page identifies API key-based authentication. Detailed key creation/permission controls need separate page check.
REST auth page inspected: REST API keys generated in WP/WooCommerce admin or app auth endpoint; read/write/read-write scopes; key access follows WordPress user capabilities.
B2C Commerce API authorization page inspected: OAuth 2.1 client scopes; JWT bearer tokens; separate setup/token paths for Shopper and Admin APIs; endpoint security scheme varies.
Integration setup page inspected: third-party integrations call REST or SOAP Web APIs; docs point to token and OAuth-based authentication. Exact current auth details need separate page check.
OAuth page inspected: OAuth 2.0; client registration submitted for review; scopes include orders, transactions, inventory, products and contacts; access is user-authorized.

SP-API onboarding page inspected: developer registration, sandbox app, authorization workflow and production application registration are distinct steps; production access is gated by onboarding/registration.
API auth page inspected: API token via x-api-token for V3/sync; analytics endpoints use query parameter token; some other hosts require contacting support for a token.

MCP docs inspected: hosted MCP at mcp.apify.com; requires Apify account and API token; Streamable HTTP with OAuth or local stdio; exposes Actors/storages/results; full-permission and rental Actors excluded.
API auth page inspected: all v1 requests use x-api-key; documented prospecting, contact/company search/enrichment and related endpoints; keys should be stored securely and rotated.

MCP docs inspected: MCP at api.clay.com/v3/mcp; OAuth with DCR self-service; signed-in user context; exposes find/enrich tools and custom functions. Public API authentication still needs separate validation.
REST authentication page inspected: personal access tokens, GitHub App tokens and GITHUB_TOKEN; token scopes/permissions affect endpoint access and authenticated rate limits.
API guide inspected: official API reference plus auth/rate-limit/pagination sections; the guide is sufficient to confirm a REST API surface but the auth detail wasn't extracted in this pass.

MCP-auth page inspected: important correction—Supabase says it does not provide MCP server functionality itself; developers can build MCP servers and use Supabase Auth OAuth 2.1/PKCE, DCR and RLS to secure them.
REST API authentication page inspected and linked to extensive Snowflake REST APIs and account/warehouse/database/table management docs. Exact supported auth methods need inspection lower on page.
API auth page inspected: bearer auth tokens; internal integration tokens and user personal tokens with scopes; OAuth2 authorization-code for third-party apps; PKCE recommended.
OAuth 2.0 page inspected: GraphQL API; OAuth app registration; read/write and granular scopes; supports PKCE; actor can be user or app.

Cloud REST API auth page inspected; this page describes basic auth with email + API token and notes it is for simple scripts/bots, not suitable for apps intended for others. OAuth 3LO needs separate review.
OAuth page inspected: OAuth authorization-code flow; apps created in developer console; user grants access; access token and refresh token; REST API integration.
Auth page inspected: personal token for individual/testing; OAuth authorization-code for apps serving others; only workspace owners/admins can create OAuth apps.
Stripe Apps OAuth page inspected: OAuth 2.0 for accessing Stripe API on behalf of users; app manifest needs OAuth access type, public distribution and explicit permissions.

Spot REST API reference inspected: REST and WebSocket surfaces, multiple base URLs and extensive product/API families. Authentication-specific section still needs validation; don't infer API-key security specifics from this page alone.

Official docs inspected: AI-agent/MCP onboarding uses API key; remote MCP SSE endpoint; documented card, balance, transactions, deposits and withdrawals tools. Highly sensitive financial actions require confirmation.
Official developer FAQ inspected: Xero MCP server and Agentic Toolkit exist; docs say MCP clients need local/STDIO support. Auth/API breadth needs separate page check.

Partner-auth page inspected: OAuth/OIDC; onboarding API uses client-credentials; other APIs use authorization-code; only clients with proper roles can grant access. Partner-specific doc, distinguish customer API path.
API page inspected: RESTful API; separate offering and standalone contract; access initiated through Direct Data team or client Plugins & Apps; connection via API key or auth token.

Public API page inspected: public API provides channels/conversations/transcripts/audio/action items/insights/workspace data; Bearer API key; only Enterprise workspaces, otherwise contact account manager.
API overview inspected: REST API; API keys generated in website settings; documented meeting/recording/team/member/user/webhook resources; rate limits stated.
MCP docs inspected: hosted MCP endpoint with Bearer API key or local server; tools include parse/extract/split/classify/edit/upload and jobs; usage/credits/rate limits are documented.
API auth page inspected: principal+token model; service-user API keys recommended for automation, PATs for human identity; service-user RBAC/scopes; enterprise and org API surfaces.

Mermaid Chart MCP docs inspected: HTTP and SSE transports; token-based auth for account integration; core validate/render tools require no auth; project/diagram management tools require authentication.
